nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Legal + regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Regulatory pack maps EU AI Act, FDA 510(k), ISO 13485, GDPR, HIPAA in a single 14-section document.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Roles, responsibilities, lines of communication are documented + clear to all personnel.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: ISO 13485 QMS section of the regulatory pack; the audit log carries the operator + clinician role on every decision record.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Policies + procedures address oversight of AI system development + deployment.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Phase 14.16 multi-agent debate + Phase 14.15 planner-revision feedback loop; both ship with deterministic-floor critics.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Organizational practices + accountability structures address AI risks.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Append-only audit + RFC 6962 Merkle tree + reproducibility SQLite archive.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms, expectations are documented.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Model Card section 1+2 (Mitchell 2019 format); datasheet motivation section.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Inter-disciplinary AI actors are involved in assessing risks and impacts.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: 4-critic ensemble (clinical_safety, fairness, evidence, llm_judge) + 3-agent debate (clinical_conservative, evidence_aggressive, fairness_guard) span clinical, statistical, ethical, ML perspectives.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Scientific integrity + Test, Evaluation, Verification + Validation (TEVV) considerations are documented.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Property-based tests, golden cohorts, adversarial v2/v3/v4 corpus, prospective synthetic eval at n=10k.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Likelihood + magnitude of impacts on individuals + society are characterised.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Subgroup audit with EOO + DP gaps; differential-privacy publication of subgroup rates (Laplace, epsilon=1.0).

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Metrics + benchmarks reflect the intended uses + context.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: ECE preferred gate <=0.05; Brier; AUROC; per-subgroup TPR + DP gaps; conformal target coverage 1-alpha.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Trustworthy characteristics (validity, safety, fairness) are measured.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Phase 16.F2 split-conformal multi-class + Pleiss 2017 calibration tension witness + selective-classification risk-coverage curve.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Risk + benefit measurements are repeated + compared over time.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Drift detection scheduler runs at configurable cadence; abstain-by-default on drift.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Treatment of AI risks is informed by ranked + documented risks.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Per-issue planner critique (Phase 14.15) emits ranked + suggested-action issue list before any tool runs.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Mechanisms are in place to deactivate, disengage, or override the AI system.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Stop-button per Article 14(4)(d) - federation exposes /admin/quiesce + abstain-trigger on uncertainty + clinician override surface.

nist_ai_rmf_rows.requirement: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented.
nist_ai_rmf_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Background scheduler runs care_gap_sweep + drift_detection; recommendation-drift tool flags per-patient changes.

oecd_ai_principles_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Subgroup audit + fairness-guard veto narrow the predicted-impact gap on under-served populations.

oecd_ai_principles_rows.requirement: Stakeholders should understand AI-based outcomes + challenge them.
oecd_ai_principles_rows.trustedrisk_evidence: Counterfactual explanations + SHAP attributions + multi-agent debate vote breakdown surfaced on every DecisionCard.

oecd_ai_principles_rows.requirement: AI systems should be robust, secure, safe throughout their entire lifecycle.

oecd_ai_principles_rows.requirement: Organizations + individuals developing or deploying AI should be accountable.
